Packing slip even had the correct plant names printed on it, which I appreciated. But when I emailed about the rot, it took nine days and three follow-ups to get a reply, and by then the third echeveria had started going the same way, spreading whatever was in that soil to the pots next to it on my sill.
label: negative

text: cover art is kinda generic, looks like every other beach-read thriller on the shelf. inside though the twist with the diary entries not matching the timeline had me flipping back to double check dates, which i never do. some side characters felt thin, the best friend barely got a personality. but the last fifty pages where it all clicks into place, especially the reveal in the attic, that part i reread twice.
label: positive

text: some of the grammar quizzes have typos in the answer key which threw me off a couple times, kinda sloppy for a paid app. but the vocabulary building through short stories is really well done, each chapter reuses words from before so nothing feels wasted, and by the end of a story arc you realize you've absorbed like 200 new words without flashcarding at all. plus the narrator voices are distinct enough you start recognizing character personalities, made me actually want to find out what happens next in a language app of all things, which says something about how the content's put together
label: positive

text: port selection skipped an sd card slot which is a hassle for my camera workflow, so i carry an adapter now. on the flip side the keyboard deck doesn't flex at all even when i'm typing aggressively, and the display's color accuracy out of the box made my photo edits translate correctly to print for the first time. speakers facing upward toward you instead of downward actually makes a real difference during video calls. fan noise is there under heavy load but it's a low hum rather than a whine. this has quietly become my main machine.
label: positive

text: Customer support took a while to answer my question about a sensor pairing glitch, and I sat on hold longer than I wanted. The eventual fix was simple, a factory reset on just the sensor, and afterward the thing performed beautifully, especially the way it ramps the furnace gradually instead of blasting hot air in one aggressive burst like our previous unit did. The weekly digest report breaking down peak usage hours has actually changed when we run the dishwasher. Watching the little screen shift from a sun icon to a soft moon graphic as evening settles in has become an oddly pleasant part of my routine.
label: positive

text: my kid wouldnt stop talking about the strawberries we bought here, said they tasted like candy lol. price was fair too, way cheaper than the grocery store and you could tell everything was picked that morning
label: positive

text: Ports are limited, just two USB-C so I'm juggling a dongle now. But the speed at which this thing wakes from sleep, instant, like it was never asleep, and exporting a 20 minute 4K video took under three minutes flat. The hinge feels like it could survive a toddler tantrum too.
label: positive

text: The receptionist remembered my name from a visit six months ago, which was a nice touch walking in. My stylist though kept getting called away to answer phones mid-cut, leaving me sitting there with wet hair for a solid ten minutes at one point. The end result was fine, nothing dramatic, but the whole appointment stretched to almost two hours for what should've been a thirty-minute trim. I had somewhere to be after and ended up rescheduling it because of the delay.
label: negative

text: Bought three of these for my kids ages 7, 9, and 12 - all different colors so they stop grabbing each other's phones. Survived being run over by a bike tire in the driveway, no exaggeration. For $16 each, that's the best money I've spent on phone accessories all year.
label: positive

text: booking online was confusing and i ended up calling twice to confirm cause the system glitched, mild headache. the actual blowout though, the volume Kayla got at my roots without it looking teased or fake, i genuinely dont know how she did it with just a round brush and some product. my usual guy was out sick so i had a rando stylist which made me nervous going in. she also gave me tips on how to recreate it myself which i immediately failed at but the intention was there lol. hair still has bounce today, two days later, which never happens for me
label: positive

text: The paperwork process took forever, lots of signing and initialing for what felt like a simple oil change. But the technician noticed my serpentine belt was fraying before I even mentioned any noise, replaced it on the spot, and now there's zero squeal on startup. Engine bay looks cleaner than it has in years too.
label: positive

text: The install video was clear and the anticipated-heating feature, which pre-warms the house before your alarm, worked exactly as described for the first couple of weeks. I also liked that it displayed local weather alongside indoor temp. But the motion sensor used for eco mode proved wildly inconsistent, sometimes assuming the house was empty while we were sitting right in the living room, dropping the temperature ten degrees without warning. Fixing it meant digging through three submenus to disable sensor-based automation entirely. Worse, a firmware rollback after one of these fixes apparently reset all our saved preferences, and I've had to reconfigure it twice since installing it four months ago.
label: negative

text: Three separate times I called to ask about my transmission repair and got put on hold for over ten minutes each time. Ended up picking up the car myself after a week because nobody would return my messages. My clutch still slips exactly like it did before.
label: negative

text: checkin line snaked outside the terminal doors and i almost missed my coffee stop, ugh. the seats though, actual legroom, my knees didn't touch anything for once. and the pilot came on the intercom just to chat about the storm system we were flying around, felt like he actually cared if we understood what was happening. landing was so smooth half the cabin clapped without anyone prompting them to
label: positive

text: toilets on deck 2 were out of order for most of the trip which is annoying when youve got a kid who needs to go every twenty minutes. the crossing itself though, man, the sunset hit right as we passed the old lighthouse and the whole deck went quiet just watching it. wifi barely worked, couldnt post anything, but who needs wifi when the sky is doing that. my daughter fell asleep on my shoulder wrapped in a blanket we bought from the gift shop, that alone made the whole day
label: positive

text: Parking cost more than the ticket and the audio guide kept glitching mid-sentence, yet the moment I turned the corner into the impressionist gallery and saw actual Monet brushstrokes up close, sunlight practically vibrating off the canvas, none of that mattered anymore.
label: positive

text: free tier is generous, i'll give it that, way more than competitors offer without paying. the interface also looks clean, not cluttered like some other budgeting apps i've tried. that said the bank linking feature has failed to refresh my accounts for the past nine days straight, just sits there spinning or throws an error code that means nothing to me. i emailed support and got a canned response about clearing cache which didn't fix anything. checked their twitter and apparently loads of people are having the same issue this month with no eta on a fix. an app that tracks money but can't actually see your money is kind of a problem.
label: negative

text: Their original series lineup surprised me, particularly a low-budget mystery show called Harrow's End that nobody talks about. Every attempt to cast to my Chromecast failed on the first try, requiring a restart of the app about half the time. Support directed me to a forum post from 2019 that no longer applied to the current version. The kids' profile locks did work well, keeping my nephew away from horror content during his visit. Then there's the ad insertion on the 'ad-free' tier I'm paying $13.49 for, three ads appeared during a single 22-minute sitcom episode last Thursday. Rewatching a show I'd already finished reset all my progress, and I had to skip through forty minutes to find where I left off. My internet is fine, 300 Mbps fiber, so the constant 'connection unstable' error message was clearly on their end.
label: negative

text: Driver took a wrong turn somewhere and texted twice asking for the gate code, yet the pad thai showed up steaming with fat shrimp and a lime wedge tucked on top like it just left the wok.
label: positive

text: Dispatch never answered the phone once the truck left, leaving me stranded without my furniture for a week.
label: negative

text: Remote access from my phone while traveling worked exactly as advertised, and I bumped the heat up before landing at O'Hare last month without any lag. The multi-zone feature is where things fell apart, since zone two consistently reports temperatures four degrees higher than what's actually in the room, based on three separate thermometers I placed there myself. I've recalibrated it twice following the manual step by step and the discrepancy hasn't budged. Paying $329 for zoning that doesn't actually zone correctly is hard to get past.
label: negative

text: We tried the 'Spy Academy' room downtown after seeing decent reviews, but the storyline made no sense once you realized two clues referenced a puzzle that had been removed in a prior renovation. Our clock read 32 minutes remaining when staff just opened the door and said 'that's basically the end anyway.' Felt cheated out of the $35 fee.
label: negative

text: The app tracker was accurate down to the minute, which almost made up for the fact that the pizza box arrived tilted, cheese slid to one corner, and the crust underneath had turned to cardboard from the grease pooling in transit.
label: negative

text: Legroom in economy was surprisingly generous, my knees weren't jammed into the seat ahead of me for once, and I noticed the safety demonstration video was actually new and not the dated one with the outdated hairstyles. Unfortunately the in-flight entertainment system froze twenty minutes in and never recovered, so I spent five hours staring at a blue error screen while the passenger beside me got his working fine, and when I flagged it down the flight attendant just told me to 'try turning it off and on' before walking away and never checking back. Boarding music was a nice touch.
label: negative

text: tanning beds are actually well maintained which surprised me, clean and the bulbs work. the contract cancellation process though is a nightmare, they made me come in person, fill out three forms, and then still charged me for an extra month claiming i missed a deadline nobody mentioned. customer service on the phone was borderline rude about it too. gotta say the juice bar smoothies are pretty good
label: negative

text: honestly expected way more for this price. hinge already feels loose after 3 weeks and theres a weird creak when i open the lid. keyboard backlight only has one brightness setting which is dumb
label: negative

text: Speakers could use more bass, sure, but the trackpad precision and that satisfying click of the keys make every writing session feel effortless.
label: positive

text: screen bezels are thicker than i expected from the photos, kind of dates the look a bit. but running two decades old excel macros without a single hiccup, and the trackpad gestures feel buttery smooth, way better than i thought a windows laptop could do. it does run a little warm on the left side near the vents when gaming. build quality though, this thing survived a drop off my desk with just a tiny scuff on the corner. keyboard layout took like a day to adjust to and now i genuinely prefer it.
label: positive

text: Binged an entire true-crime docuseries last weekend and never once dealt with buffering, even streaming to three devices simultaneously in the house. The skip-recap feature saves real time when you're plowing through a season in one sitting. I appreciated that canceling for a month during a busy work stretch was painless, and my watchlist was exactly as I left it when I resubscribed. Audio syncing on foreign films has been flawless, unlike a competitor I used last year. This is now my default before checking anything else.
label: positive

text: There was a stretch in the middle where the room went quiet for too long between puzzles, nothing pointing us anywhere, and we just wandered a bit. That said, the pirate ship set was something else, the floor actually tilted slightly when you stepped on certain boards, and the treasure chest puzzle where you had to align three brass rings to match a tattooed map on a mannequin's arm was genuinely clever. Finding the false-bottomed barrel with the second key hidden in sand was a highlight, and the cannon prop that fired confetti when we solved the final combination got a genuine laugh out of everyone. The hint system took a minute to respond once, which cost us maybe ninety seconds, but the ship's wheel puzzle at the end, where turning it revealed a trapdoor beneath the mast, was the kind of payoff you don't forget.
label: positive

text: Battery usage dropped noticeably after switching to this app's dark mode widget on my home screen.
label: positive

text: the boarding music was way too loud and my seatmate had this cough the entire flight, not great combo for a six hour trip. what saved it was breakfast, this simple little egg dish that had no business being that good on a plane, i went back for seconds and they just gave it to me no questions asked. sun came up right as we were over the ocean, this thin line of pink stretching the whole horizon, i took like twenty photos on my phone like a tourist
label: positive

text: asked for a simple button replacement and somehow they used a totally different color button that doesnt match at all. didnt notice till i got home, wasnt about to drive back for that
label: negative

text: After moving into a drafty 1920s bungalow, I wasn't sure any smart device could handle the quirks of ancient ductwork, but the adaptive recovery feature figured out how long my system needs to preheat the house and adjusted the schedule accordingly. Within two weeks, mornings stopped starting with a cold shock. The app's energy report broke down usage by day and let me spot that my furnace was running longer on windy days, prompting me to finally seal a drafty window. Pairing it with my smart speaker was seamless, and now I just say a room name to adjust things without getting off the couch.
label: positive

text: Walking into the pirate ship set was a fun moment, complete with a rocking floor effect that sold the illusion well. From there, though, the whole experience became a scavenger hunt for batteries, since three separate props required flashlights that had clearly not been changed in weeks. We spent more time hunting under fake barrels for spare AAs than actually solving anything. The treasure chest reveal at the end was satisfying in theory, but by that point we'd used four of our five hints just to get equipment working, and the game master's response over the radio was a flat 'yeah that happens sometimes.'
label: negative

text: Filing my return took under twenty minutes once I sat down, and the software they used auto-filled most of my W-2 info without me typing a thing. But getting to that appointment was its own ordeal — I called three times over two weeks and left messages that were never returned, finally showing up in person just to book a slot. Then, after everything was filed, I got a notice from the state saying my address on file didn't match my return, an error that apparently happened because the preparer copied from an old file instead of asking me directly. Correcting it required me to mail in a form myself since nobody at the office could resend it electronically.
label: negative

text: noise level is a bit much when you first turn it on, my dog bolts to the other room every time lol. but that power translates into actually lifting dirt out of grout lines on my kitchen tile, which nothing else i've owned has ever done. plus the cord retracts with one button, this satisfying whirring sound, no more tripping over it or wrapping it by hand
label: positive

text: What impressed me most was how the service handled a full household migration when we moved apartments last month—watch history, downloaded content, and even my paused episode of a nine-season sitcom transferred without a hitch onto the new router. Streaming in 4K on the new smart TV showed noticeably crisper detail during dark scenes than my old provider ever managed. The parental control settings take a few extra taps to adjust, but everything else has been refreshingly seamless.
label: positive

text: Loved that they had a TV on the ceiling with actual decent shows, small thing but it helped. The exam itself felt rushed though, like six minutes tops, and he didn't mention the chipped tooth I specifically came in about until I brought it up myself. Now I've got a follow-up scheduled that should've just been handled that day.
label: negative

text: The guy at the counter walked me through paper stock options until we found one that fit my budget.
label: positive

text: Their apple cider donuts were warm and cinnamon-dusted, but the card reader ate my payment twice, the vendor blamed my bank, and I spent twenty minutes on hold with my bank untangling the duplicate charge.
label: negative

text: The restroom was tucked oddly behind the coat check, easy to miss on a first visit, and the line for it backed up during the rush. None of that mattered much once the scallops came out, seared to a deep gold crust and set over a corn puree that tasted like it had been made from corn picked that very morning, with a scattering of trout roe adding little bursts of salt. Our appetizer took a while longer than the entrees, oddly enough, arriving almost alongside them. The espresso martini at the end, shaken tableside with real theater, more than made up for the timing hiccup, and I left already planning who I'd bring back next.
label: positive

text: Bindings on my rental skis released unexpectedly twice on a mellow green run, which felt unsafe rather than just annoying. When I brought it up at the counter, the tech barely looked up from his phone and said 'probably just cold weather doing that.' Paid $80 for two days and won't trust their equipment again.
label: negative

text: One bud is noticeably quieter than the other, so I'm constantly cranking volume just to balance them out. Contacted support and got a canned response that didn't fix anything. Waste of money honestly.
label: negative

text: Six months in and this kettle still looks brand new despite daily abuse from my chaotic kitchen. The temperature presets are the real win here, I can nail the exact heat for green tea without guessing anymore. Just don't overfill it past the max line or it sputters a little.
label: positive

text: I liked the length, it hits mid-thigh so my jeans stayed dry during a downpour in Chicago. But the DWR coating wore off after maybe four washes, even though I followed the care label exactly and used the recommended Nikwax spray afterward. Now water just sits on the shoulders in beads for a second before soaking straight through. The chest pocket zipper also snagged the lining fabric on day three, and there's a permanent pucker there now that catches on itself every time I try to close it.
label: negative

text: Meals for the week ran about $11.50 per serving, cheaper than most delivery apps I'd been using. The packaging generated an enormous amount of trash, six ice packs and four separate plastic sleeves for a single dinner. One recipe, a supposedly simple pasta primavera, took nearly 50 minutes instead of the listed 25 because of unclear knife-cut instructions. Skipping a week required navigating through five different screens before the option even appeared, and I nearly got charged for a delivery I didn't want. The garlic butter shrimp scampi from the first week was actually excellent.
label: negative

text: The espresso machine hissed and sputtered like it was on its last leg, and I waited nearly ten minutes past what I'd normally tolerate. But then the barista set down a flat white with a rosette so precise it looked stenciled, the foam dense and sweet, the espresso underneath tasting of dark chocolate and toasted hazelnut. Sunlight came through the front window and hit the marble counter just right, and the guy next to me was tapping away on a laptop, completely absorbed, like he'd found his office. My oat milk substitution cost an extra seventy cents, a little annoying, but I barely thought about it once that first sip hit.
label: positive

text: The lobby staff were sweet and offered snacks while I waited. My preparer, though, entered my mortgage interest in the wrong box, which triggered an IRS letter two months later that I had to spend an entire Saturday sorting out on hold with them.
label: negative

text: The lock on the second cabinet stuck twice and someone had to jiggle it with a hairpin the game master handed through the door, minor annoyance in the moment. But that library room, with the shelves that rotated to reveal the hidden study and the globe that lit up constellations matching the star chart on the wall, had us buzzing for the rest of the night. The final puzzle involved cross-referencing three separate ciphers under a blacklight, and when the bookshelf finally swung open to reveal the safe, four of us actually cheered out loud. One puzzle near the middle felt like padding, just a word search that didn't connect to anything else. Still thinking about how the ink stamps glowed under the UV flashlight days later.
label: positive

text: Packing day started fine, with the crew wrapping dishes in paper and taping boxes with actual care. Where things fell apart was the labeling system, which apparently meant writing 'kitchen' on some boxes and nothing at all on others. We ended up with cooking utensils in the bathroom, a lamp in with the pots, and to this day the box containing my grandmother's wedding china has never turned up, not in the truck, not in storage, nowhere.
label: negative

text: I'll admit the hydrangea itself was healthy and full of buds, but the stake it was tied to had snapped in shipping and gouged a hole clean through the pot, spilling half the soil into the box and leaving roots dangling exposed for who knows how long.
label: negative

text: Directions for the yogurt-making function are buried on page 14 of a booklet that otherwise reads clearly, so I nearly gave up before figuring it out. Once I did, though, the fermentation setting produced yogurt with the tang and thickness of the Greek stuff I used to buy for $6 a tub. The cooking bowl is a bit heavier than I expected, awkward to lift out one-handed while balancing a toddler. Rice made in the standard white rice mode comes out consistently fluffy, tested it against my sister's older model side by side and hers was noticeably stickier. The power cord retracts oddly and sometimes needs a second push to fully store.
label: positive

text: Sound is crisp enough out of the box, but the right bud started cutting out during calls after week two and now drops entirely if I turn my head too fast.
label: negative

text: My book club argued for almost two hours about the unreliable narrator twist, which tells you everything about how well this thing is constructed. The prose gets a bit purple during the storm chapters, sure, but the payoff at the reunion scene made everyone forgive that instantly. Bringing snacks next time because we clearly need the extra time to talk.
label: positive

text: he cut it a little close on my waist first go round, had to bring it back in for the trousers. no big deal in the end though bc when he redid the taper on my blazer sleeves, the way the cuff sat right at my wristbone was honestly the best fit ive had from any tailor in this city. even matched the button spacing to my other jackets without me asking.
label: positive

text: Paid six bucks for a pint of strawberries and half of them were moldy at the bottom. Asking for a refund got me an eye roll and a mumbled excuse about 'that's how they come.' Total letdown honestly.
label: negative

text: These arrived with a factory defect in the left earbud that produced a constant high-pitched whine whenever I raised the volume above 50%. I requested a replacement through the retailer and waited eleven days for a response, then another two weeks for the new pair, which had the exact same issue. At that point I just asked for a refund instead of gambling a third time.
label: negative

text: The rooftop pool was the real MVP of this trip, especially at sunset with a drink in hand. Room service showed up in under 15 minutes every single time we ordered, which honestly floored me. Only gripe is the elevator got crowded during checkout rush, but that's a small thing to complain about.
label: positive

text: Setup was quick and the display colors looked accurate out of the box, but the webcam smears every video call into a blurry mess and support just told me to update drivers that don't exist yet.
label: negative

text: Setup took one tap and they auto-connected to my phone before I even opened the case fully, which felt like magic after years of manual pairing. The touch sensor on the left bud occasionally misfires during jaw movement, like when I'm chewing gum. Everything else though, the punchy mids, the way podcasts sound like the host is sitting across from me, makes we reach for these before any other pair I own.
label: positive

text: the tomato seedlings looked healthy enough in the pics they sent before shipping. got here in like 4 days which aint bad. thing is the box got crushed on one side and half the little stakes holding stuff up snapped, so three plants were just flopped over onto each other, stems bent at weird angles. tried to prop them back up but one just wont stand straight anymore, kind of leaning like its tired of life. customer service girl was polite when i emailed tho
label: negative

text: My late-night arrival was met with a warm cookie and quick check-in, erasing any travel exhaustion instantly.
label: positive

text: Six weeks of waiting for a 'ready to ship' hydrangea collection, only to receive an email saying the order was cancelled due to inventory issues. No explanation why it took six weeks to figure that out, and the refund still hasn't posted to my card despite two follow-up calls.
label: negative

text: The paper stock for my resume booklets had a nice weight to it, thick enough to feel substantial without being stiff. Where things fell apart was the trimming, since the edges were noticeably uneven page to page, off by what looked like a sixteenth of an inch in places, giving the whole stack a slightly crooked look when squared on a table. I mentioned it at pickup and was told a machine was 'due for calibration,' which didn't make me feel great about the twenty copies already in hand.
label: negative

text: price was actually really reasonable for the route and i got a window seat without even requesting one. flight attendants handed out blankets which was a nice surprise on a chilly plane. but then we circled the airport for almost an hour bc of 'traffic' before landing, burning who knows how much fuel and patience, and the guy next to me kept coughing without covering his mouth the entire time which was honestly disgusting to sit next to for 6 hours straight with nowhere to move
label: negative

text: The line to get in stretched onto the sidewalk, and standing there for twenty-five minutes without a menu to look at got a little old. Inside, the noise level was intense, hard to hear my brother across the table. That said, the tacos al pastor came stacked with pineapple that had clearly been caramelized on the same grill as the pork, and the char on both mixed into every bite. The guacamole, made tableside, had lime zest folded through it that most places skip. My brother's margarita was watered down, but mine, the mezcal one with the smoked salt rim, tasted like someone actually cared about the recipe. We ended up ordering a second round of the elote just to keep the flavor going a little longer.
label: positive

text: Delivery landed right at 8am like they promised, box insulation kept the steak cold despite the 85-degree afternoon it sat waiting for me. The recipe called for two tablespoons of a spice blend that wasn't included in the box at all, forcing an emergency substitution with whatever paprika I had left. Billing charged me for six meals the week I'd paused my subscription, and the refund didn't post until I called twice, on a Thursday and then again the following Monday. The dessert kit brownie mix, at least, turned out rich and fudgy.
label: negative

text: Locker room's a bit tight and the paint's peeling near the showers, but the squat racks are brand new, the staff know my name, and the 5am crowd makes the whole thing feel like a second home.
label: positive

text: Dropped off three dress shirts for tapering at Charlie's on Main, paid $18 per shirt, and picked them up Monday morning exactly as promised. The collar work was crisp and even, no puckering at all. Wish they had evening hours, but the quality made up for it.
label: positive

text: Ordered three hydrangeas and what showed up looked like they'd been through a hailstorm, half the leaves shredded and stems bent sideways. The packing slip even said 'inspected for quality' which is laughable. Won't be back for round two.
label: negative

text: Left three voicemails about a botched flyer order and never once got a callback.
label: negative

text: Half my kitchen boxes never made it onto the truck and they blamed the warehouse.
label: negative

text: My flight from Denver was delayed ninety minutes because of a de-icing backlog, which meant missing my connection window by a hair. The gate agent, a woman named Priya, rebooked me onto a nonstop two hours later at no charge and handed me a $12 meal voucher without me even asking. The new seat was 22C, aisle, extra legroom for the same fare. By the time I landed in Austin, I'd had a full dinner, a nap, and a surprisingly good espresso from the galley cart.
label: positive

text: The magnetic snap for car mounts is what sold me. Installed my Anker mount in the truck and the phone locks in place instantly every morning commute. Case adds minimal bulk, maybe 2mm, and the buttons still click properly after 3 weeks of daily use.
label: positive

text: the offline download feature saved me on a long flight, grabbed a season before takeoff no problem. that said the account sharing limit dropped from five screens to two with zero warning, my whole family group chat blew up over it that same week. autoplay previews blast audio at full volume the second you hover over a thumbnail, scared me half to death more than once late at night. and the search function is basically useless, typed a full show title and got unrelated horror movies instead. downloads work though, gotta give it that.
label: negative

text: Bought this for my kid's soccer games since I stand on the sideline no matter the weather, and it's kept me warm and dry through some brutal October matches. The length covers my hips nicely so no water sneaks up from below. Wish it came in a darker color, but that's just my taste.
label: positive

text: speakers sound like theyre coming from inside a tin can, tinny and quiet even at max volume. also the charger cable is way too short, barely reaches my outlet from the couch. little things add up
label: negative

text: The office smelled strongly of antiseptic and the magazines were from 2019, still the orthodontist adjusted my retainer with such careful precision that my bite finally clicked into perfect alignment for the first time in years.
label: positive

text: I appreciated the historical detail about the shipyards, but then the romance subplot gets resolved via a letter that contradicts something the character said two chapters earlier.
label: negative

text: checked in friday and the guy at the front desk was super friendly, gave us extra firewood no charge. the tent pad itself though was on a slope so bad our sleeping bags kept sliding into the corner all night, i woke up basically folded against the tent wall. also whoever designed the fire pit clearly never lit an actual fire, it filled with smoke every time and theres no ventilation gap at the bottom. my clothes still smell like it three washes later. the little store sells decent ice cream at least. wifi at the office worked fine for checking messages
label: negative

text: gotta say the tray table wasnt wobbly for once lol small win but it matters. flight attendant named marco kept refilling coffee without me even asking twice. bathroom stayed clean the entire 5 hour flight which is basically a miracle these days
label: positive

text: Tire pressure was left a touch low when I picked it up, but the new cables make the brake levers feel tight and responsive with barely a squeeze.
label: positive

text: Sheets were crisp, the shower pressure was strong, and the concierge recommended a taxi driver who got us to the airport in record time. I'll give them that. But the air conditioning unit rattled like a dying appliance every time it kicked on, which was constantly, since the room held heat like a greenhouse. We called maintenance twice; someone came, poked at it, and left it exactly as loud as before. By the second night we were sleeping with pillows over our heads, and the rattling is honestly the only thing I can still hear when I think about this trip.
label: negative

text: The estimate over the phone didn't include a flight of stairs I mentioned twice, so the final cost crept higher than expected. There was also a slightly awkward moment when they showed up without enough tape and had to run to a store nearby. Once they got going, though, it was clear these guys knew furniture. They wrapped my leather sofa in stretch film so tight it looked shrink-wrapped, then carried it down three flights without a single scuff on the walls. The lead mover spent extra time securing my aquarium stand with extra padding, even though it wasn't fragile cargo in the traditional sense, just because he could tell I was nervous about it. Watching them slide my refrigerator through a doorway with an inch of clearance on either side, I stopped thinking about the tape run entirely.
label: positive

text: The bathtub had a crack running straight through it and water pooled on the floor after every shower. Wifi dropped every ten minutes, made working remotely impossible. Front desk shrugged and said 'that's just how it is here.'
label: negative

text: Cabin smelled faintly of diesel near the loading deck, but up top the wind off the strait carried salt spray straight into my face while gulls wheeled level with the railing and the coastline unrolled in slow green folds for two hours.
label: positive

text: Dropped off my terrier who hates baths and picked up a dog who seemed genuinely happy, tail wagging the whole ride home. They also filed down his nails so short I haven't heard him click on the floor since. Great with nervous dogs, clearly.
label: positive

text: the location is unbeatable, five minute walk from my apartment and open 24 hours which i use a lot. but the sauna's been 'temporarily closed' for four months now with just a sign taped to the door, no updates ever. equipment maintenance is slow too, saw a torn cable on the lat pulldown machine sit there for three weeks before anyone touched it. staff at the desk are friendly enough when you catch them, always smiling
label: negative

text: navigation between profiles is smooth, my kid can find her cartoons without me touching it. the actual encoding quality tanks the second more than one device streams in the house, picture turns to mush and stays that way till someone logs off. i counted four separate outages this month alone, one lasted almost the whole evening during a show finale i'd been waiting weeks for. recommendations algorithm just shows me the same eight titles no matter how many i mark not interested. profile switching is genuinely painless at least.
label: negative

text: signed up mainly for the language lessons and the gamification aspect is fun, streaks keep me coming back most days. voice recognition for pronunciation practice also works better than i expected going in. the problem is the app logged me out three times this week for no clear reason, each time losing my daily progress and resetting a streak i'd built up for over a month. support said it's a known bug they're working on but gave no timeline whatsoever. also the ads before each lesson have gotten longer recently, sometimes over thirty seconds now. losing a month long streak to a login bug kind of kills the motivation the gamification was supposed to build.
label: negative

text: Snack bar was overpriced and the coffee tasted like it had been sitting since morning. But the horizon out past the stern turned this deep orange as the sun dropped, clouds catching fire for a solid ten minutes, and everyone on deck just went quiet watching it.
label: positive

text: Membership pricing went up in January without much warning, which stung a little. That aside, the 24-hour access has fundamentally changed my relationship with exercise, since I can go at 11pm after a late shift and have the whole cardio section to myself, machines all in working order and quiet enough to actually think. The cleaning crew misses corners under the benches sometimes. But the personal trainers here don't just hand you a laminated sheet, they actually watch you lift and adjust in real time, and mine caught a shoulder imbalance that had been bothering me for months before I even mentioned it.
label: positive

text: Six weeks in and my lower back pain from that old spring mattress has completely vanished.
label: positive

text: My wife's salmon at $28 was overcooked to the point of falling apart into flakes of dust. We arrived at 6:40 on a Tuesday, barely half full, yet service was glacial. Our waiter Dennis vanished for twenty minutes after taking our order. Skip this place.
label: negative

text: Six bridesmaid dresses needed alterations before a wedding, and somehow he had all of them hemmed, bustled, and fitted within four days flat. Each dress had different fabric—chiffon, satin, lace overlay—and he adjusted his technique for every single one without a single pucker or uneven seam showing up in photos.
label: positive

text: Bloatware took me almost an hour to fully uninstall after unboxing, which felt like a rough start. Once cleared out though, this thing flies through video editing exports way faster than my old machine ever did, and the hinge design lets me flip it into tablet mode without any weird wobble. Bottom edge gets a little sharp against the wrist during long sessions, but that vivid OLED panel makes every photo edit look genuinely professional.
label: positive

text: Their dessert add-on, a $6.99 tiramisu kit, was excellent and came together in fifteen minutes. Main courses are another story: the pesto pasta kit's basil had visibly wilted and blackened before I even opened the bag, and the pine nuts sachet was missing entirely, not just short a few, gone. I emailed photos to support and got a canned response about 'quality checks' with no real fix offered. Shipping is fast, I'll give them that, arriving within the promised two-day window from their Ohio facility.
label: negative

text: Customer service on the phone was a little curt when I called to confirm details, almost brusque. In person, though, the two movers who showed up, Ben and Cory, were nothing like that. They took extra time wrapping my grandmother's oil paintings in cardboard corners, stacked my moving boxes in the truck like a puzzle so nothing shifted, and carried an oversized sectional through a doorway that barely cleared by inches. The whole job, quoted at $430, came in exactly on price. Seeing that couch make it through the door without a single scuff on the frame is the story I've told at every dinner party since.
label: positive

text: The bathhouse near loop C had standing water on the floor the entire three days we stayed, and one of the two shower stalls was simply locked with a hand-written 'out of order since June' sign still taped up. Raccoons got into our cooler the first night because the site lacked the promised animal-proof bin, tearing through a bag of bread and scattering wrappers across the neighbor's tent pad. Staff shrugged when I reported it, saying wildlife is 'just part of camping here.' For $65 a night I expected basic sanitation at minimum.
label: negative

text: Box packaging kept things cold well past the six-hour transit time, which impressed me initially. The dealbreaker came with the pork carnitas kit: the recipe card pictured shredded pork but the cut inside was a solid, bone-in shoulder piece I had no tools or instructions to break down properly. I spent an extra 45 minutes just prepping meat that should've arrived ready to go. Then the following week's charge came in at $71.40, higher than the $59.99 I signed up for, with no explanation of the price change anywhere in my account settings.
label: negative

text: I'll say this: the wine list was extensive and the sommelier gave a genuinely thoughtful recommendation that paired beautifully with my starter. The starter itself, a beet salad, was fresh and well-balanced. From there, though, things went sideways. My main course, a duck breast, arrived so overcooked that the meat had turned the texture of shoe leather, gray throughout with no trace of pink. The accompanying potatoes were cold, clearly plated well before the duck was ready. Our server disappeared for a solid half hour after taking our order, leaving us to flag down a passing busser just to get more water. When I mentioned the duck issue, the kitchen sent out a replacement that took another twenty-five minutes, by which point everyone else at the table had finished eating. The manager comped a single glass of wine as an apology, which felt thin given the wait.
label: negative

text: four different profiles for my family and each kid gets their own weird recommendation algorithm which is kinda hilarious but also super convenient, no more arguing over whats appropriate to watch. parental controls actually work unlike other apps ive tried. would recommend to anyone with young kids
label: positive

text: the onboard cafe ran out of food an hour into a 6 hour ride, so we just sat there hungry watching staff eat their own lunch break meals
label: negative

text: The components are genuinely gorgeous, thick tiles and minis that feel expensive in your hands. Setup ate almost forty minutes though, and once we finally started, the rulebook contradicted itself twice on how resource tokens convert, so we had to guess and just hope we guessed the same way each time. My friend group basically sat there flipping through pages while the pizza got cold.
label: negative

text: Booked the 2pm timed slot online and still waited 40 minutes in a line that wrapped around the block. Once inside, three of the interactive displays in the children's wing had 'Out of Order' signs taped to them, including the one my kid was most excited about. Staff at the front desk seemed annoyed when I asked for a refund on the audio guide rental. The Delacroix room was nice, but that's the only thing I'd praise about the Renwick Gallery.
label: negative

text: The boat rocked more than I expected and I had to sit down for a bit to steady my stomach. That passed quickly enough, and soon I was up on deck again watching the shoreline unfold, little fishing shacks and colorful roofs stacking up the hillside like something painted. Charging ports were broken at my seat, minor annoyance, but the way the horn echoed off the cliffs as we approached the dock gave me chills in the best way.
label: positive

text: Loved the native speaker audio clips, they sound natural instead of robotic like a lot of these apps. Unfortunately the subscription auto-renewed at double the price I originally signed up for, no email warning, nothing. I only noticed because my bank flagged the charge as suspicious.
label: negative

text: the waiting room coffee machine was broken which whatever, i had my laptop anyway. what got me was carlos actually road tested the brakes twice before calling it done, even adjusted the parking brake cable without charging extra. took like an hour longer than promised but he walked me through the whole invoice line by line and pointed out i didnt need the cabin filter replaced yet, saved me like 40 bucks right there
label: positive

text: Legroom was surprisingly decent for economy, though the crew served the meal so late that half the cabin had already fallen asleep and woke up hungry at landing.
label: negative

text: Ordering custom stickers here involved an initial proof that had the wrong die-cut shape, forcing a second round of approval emails that ate up a day. When the corrected batch arrived, the vinyl held up against water exposure during a trip I hadn't even planned for, and the colors stayed vibrant after months of being slapped on a laptop lid that travels everywhere with me. The adhesive backing peeled cleanly without any residue, and honestly the registration on the multicolor design was tighter than stickers I've gotten from bigger online services charging twice as much.
label: positive

text: The heirloom tomatoes stacked in mismatched crates first caught my eye, but it was the vendor's willingness to slice one open on the spot that sealed the deal. Deep purple flesh, barely any seeds, and a sweetness that made me buy four pounds. A tiny gripe: no bags larger than the small paper ones, so I had to juggle tomatoes in my arms to the car.
label: positive

text: Waited 45 minutes past my pickup time only to find the flyers stapled crooked and half of them smudged.
label: negative

text: Free wifi, quiet corners, and a barista who remembered my usual after one visit—can't ask for more.
label: positive

text: the ramp loading took forever and we sat in the car for almost 40 minutes before boarding even started. once we got settled tho, i went up to the open deck and just felt the whole trip shift, salty air, gulls circling, this old guy playing guitar near the vending machines which was such a nice random touch. blankets they handed out were kind of thin honestly. but curling up with one anyway while watching the harbor lights fade out was one of those quiet moments i didnt expect to get from a ferry ride
label: positive

text: I like that it goes low enough for my kid to use too, but the control panel started double-clicking last week and now it randomly jumps three inches while I'm mid-sentence in meetings.
label: negative

text: The estimate quoted over the phone was $1,200. The final bill came to $2,850, padded with 'stair fees,' a 'long carry charge' for a driveway that was maybe fifteen feet long, and a mysterious 'fuel surcharge' that wasn't mentioned anywhere in the contract. When I called to dispute it, the office manager just kept repeating that I'd signed the paperwork, ignoring that the paperwork was shoved at me while three guys stood around waiting to unload my couch onto the sidewalk.
label: negative

text: My kid actually finished her multiplication homework because the flashcard streaks kept her hooked for a solid week.
label: positive

text: webcam quality is genuinely embarrassing, looks like im on a call from 2009. grainy even in good lighting. also storage fills up so fast bc theres barely any usable space out of the box
label: negative

text: The queue to check in ran a few minutes behind, which ate into some of our chat time beforehand, a small thing but worth mentioning. Inside, the wizard's tower theme was full of small delights, like a bookshelf where pulling the right spellbook triggered a hidden latch, and a cauldron that bubbled with dry ice fog right as we solved the potion-mixing puzzle. The astrolabe puzzle, where aligning three rings revealed a hidden message etched underneath, took real teamwork and had us talking through it out loud the whole time. A rune-matching puzzle near the end felt a little arbitrary, more about brute-forcing combinations than actual logic. But the moment the tower door unlocked with a mechanical groan and false stars twinkled on the ceiling above us as we stepped out, felt like the perfect send-off to the whole adventure.
label: positive

text: Password sharing crackdowns made me grumble for a week. Still, the kids' profile with genuinely smart content filtering, combined with bedtime auto-dim screen mode, means my toddler watches age-appropriate cartoons while I binge true crime documentaries with commentary from actual retired detectives.
label: positive

text: Ebike maintenance felt intimidating to seek out, but this shop handled the motor connections and battery contacts alongside the usual drivetrain cleaning without missing a beat. They tightened a rattling fender bracket I'd been meaning to deal with myself and never got around to. Communication throughout was clear, including a call before doing anything beyond the basic tune-up. Riding to work now is noticeably quieter and more confident.
label: positive

text: Subtitles lag two seconds behind the dialogue on literally every foreign film I've tried.
label: negative

text: my sister dragged me here bc she wouldnt stop raving about the lavender honey latte and now i get it, it tasted like drinking a warm garden without being too sweet. the guy at the counter drew a little sun in the foam which felt unnecessary but cute. seating was tight during rush hour but they had a back patio i didnt know about that fixed everything
label: positive

text: Their hand-stitched buttonholes on my coat are the kind of detail you only notice once you own one.
label: positive

text: ok so i wasnt expecting much but the offline download feature saved my flight, watched 3 movies with zero buffering. picture quality on my old tablet was surprisingly crisp too. only gripe is the search bar is a lil slow but whatever, im hooked
label: positive

text: I noticed a small scuff on the hallway baseboard afterward, probably from the dolly wheels, nothing a bit of paint won't fix. The estimate call took longer than expected, almost thirty minutes of going through inventory, but that thoroughness paid off because the final price matched the quote exactly: $740, no surprise fees. The two movers, Sam and his partner, wrapped my flat-screen TV in a custom cardboard sleeve I didn't even know they carried and strapped it securely so it never shifted during transport. They also managed to get my washer and dryer down a narrow basement staircase that two previous companies had refused to attempt, using furniture sliders to ease them around the tight corner without a single dent.
label: positive

text: gonna be honest i almost returned it thinking the screen was too glossy but after a week the brightness and sharpness won me over for reading pdfs all day. typing for hours doesnt hurt my wrists like my old machine did. wifi grabs signal even in the basement which shocked me
label: positive

text: the world building at the start is genuinely creative, loved the market scenes early on. but the middle act introduces like four new characters at once and i genuinely lost track of who was who, had to flip back constantly. theres also a continuity error where a character is described as dead and then just shows up two chapters later with zero acknowledgment, editor really missed that one. ending felt tacked on too, like they needed to hit a page count.
label: negative

text: Cleaning the steam vent takes a bit of fiddly disassembly, and I misplaced the little cap twice before finding it wedged under the fridge. That aside, the sushi rice setting produces grains with this glossy, almost translucent sheen, perfectly separated but still sticky enough to hold shape when I roll it. The digital display is bright enough to read from across the kitchen even with the lights dimmed, and the auto-shutoff clicks over so smoothly that I never worry about burning a pot again.
label: positive

text: The dialogue between the two sisters in chapter three is sharp and funny, real back-and-forth energy. Past that though, the plot relies on a coincidence so large, a long-lost letter surfacing exactly when needed, that it undercuts everything built before it. Secondary characters like the neighbor Frank get introduced with detail and then vanish for two hundred pages before reappearing with no explanation. The paperback cover art is lovely, moody and blue, but the glue on mine failed after a single trip in a beach bag.
label: negative

text: Hit a pothole hard enough to bend my rim and throw off my alignment, and I was dreading the cost given how specialized rim repair can be. The shop had a guy, Owen, who does wheel straightening in-house rather than outsourcing it, which saved me roughly $150 compared to two other quotes I'd gotten. The alignment afterward was spot on, no more pulling to the right on the highway. Scheduling took a few days since they were busy, but the actual repair itself was fast and clearly done with care.
label: positive

text: We played this at a coworker's housewarming and somehow ended up staying two extra hours because nobody wanted to stop. The auction phase creates this delicious tension where everyone's second-guessing their budget. My only quibble is the player count sweet spot feels narrower than the box suggests.
label: positive

text: Sure, the 4K picture on the nature docs looks incredible and the app loads fast on my TV. But three times this week it just logged me out mid-episode and made me redo the password with that awful remote typing. Then when I finally got back in, it had lost my spot and started the episode from zero.
label: negative

text: Three separate visits later, the same check engine light still flickers on every morning.
label: negative

text: Fifteen-year-old touring bike, and I wasn't sure it was worth fixing up versus replacing. The shop disagreed and proved it by overhauling the hubs, replacing worn-out bar tape, and dialing in the front derailleur that had been rubbing for months. Everything feels tight and responsive again. Glad I didn't give up on this frame.
label: positive

text: My electric bill has been the same fight every winter for a decade, and this device finally gave me leverage. It learns your patterns within the first week and starts nudging the schedule to match, so by day nine it had figured out I like the house cooler at 6am for my run and warmer by 7pm. The remote sensor I placed in the basement corrected years of temperature imbalance between floors. Setup required a C-wire adapter since my old furnace didn't have one, but the included part solved that without a trip to the hardware store.
label: positive

text: Took these on a flight to Chicago and the passive noise isolation alone knocked out most of the engine hum before I even turned on ANC. Microphone picks up some wind noise if I'm outside, learned that the hard way during a call on my porch. Fit is snug, almost too snug for the first hour, then it settled in nicely. Tap controls for skipping tracks worked every single time, no missed inputs like my last pair. Sound quality on podcasts, especially voice clarity, stayed crisp for the entire four-hour flight.
label: positive

text: Shipped with a coating that started peeling off the palm rest within two weeks of normal use.
label: negative

text: free wifi in the waiting room and decent coffee, small things but i noticed. the actual work is another story, my ac still blows warm on one side after they charged me $200 to fix exactly that problem. called back and they said it might need a second visit for more diagnostics, more money basically. so now im sweating in traffic wondering if i just paid for nothing
label: negative

text: The honey jars weren't sealed properly and mine leaked all over my tote bag on the walk home. Sticky mess aside, the woman working the booth couldn't answer basic questions about which flowers the bees pollinated. Kind of defeats the purpose of buying local, right?
label: negative

text: The paperwork checklist they emailed was confusing and out of order, but sitting across from someone who actually explained why my crypto losses offset my capital gains made the whole afternoon feel like money well spent.

text: Loading went quickly, the crew hustled the couch, mattress, and dresser out in under an hour, and they were friendly the whole time. The trouble came when they swung the couch around a hallway corner and gouged a chunk out of the drywall down to the paper backing. I asked if they could note it for a damage claim, and the lead mover said that wasn't something he handled and to call the office instead. The office, when I finally reached them, said no incident report existed for our move.

text: my appointment got bumped twice because they overbooked, ended up sitting in the lobby for like 40 mins with no explanation. when i finally sat down the guy doing my hair kept getting calls and stepping away mid cut. so unprofessional honestly
label: negative

text: I like that the widget updates in real time on my home screen. What kills it is the app eating like 20% of my battery just sitting in the background doing nothing, and I've had to start force-closing it manually after every use.
label: negative

text: The cord is shorter than I expected, so it forced me to rearrange my counter setup near an outlet I don't usually use. The buttons have a satisfying tactile click, and the whole unit is quiet enough that I've left it running in the next room during a video call without anyone noticing.

text: Ticket machine ate my card and made me chase down a crew member for a manual receipt, so I ended up leaning on the bow rail as porpoises cut alongside the hull for a solid five minutes.

text: Sure, the honey stick was a nice free sample, yet the same jar of jam sat on the table three weeks running with a thickening film of dust, and the price scrawled on masking tape had been crossed out and rewritten four times.

text: Wore this on a three-day backpacking trip in the Smokies and never once felt a drop get through, even during that sideways downpour on day two. text: The guy filing my return misspelled my last name, and now I'm stuck untangling a mess with the IRS.

label: positive

text: Certain lessons repeat the same example sentences three units in a row, which gets tedious. The app's offline mode let me keep drilling flashcards during a subway commute with zero signal, and the vocabulary stuck because the images paired with each word were oddly specific and memorable.

text: I could have spent the whole afternoon in the ceramics room alone, the glazes on those Ming vases were extraordinary up close. text: The magnetic ring is a touch weak with heavier mounts, though the texture on the back reads like brushed metal under my thumb and it's shielded my phone through four separate face-down falls onto the bathroom tile.

text: Tip suggestion was reasonable and checkout took ten seconds, but the pad thai had clumped into a cold, oily tangle and the peanuts on top had gone soft from sitting under the lid too long.
label: negative

text: The interface looks polished and the daily goal tracker kept me motivated for a while, but then the speech-recognition engine started marking correct Italian answers as wrong around unit four, the in-app chat with tutors lagged so badly messages arrived in the wrong order, and I never got a refund for the week it was unusable.
label: negative

text: Non-slip feet on the bottom are thinner than the rubber pads on my old cooker, so it inches slightly on my laminate counter during the spin cycle. The tamale setting, though, something I didn't expect to use much, has become my Sunday ritual, producing masa that holds together perfectly after forty minutes of steaming. Manual only includes recipes in one language despite claiming otherwise on the box. Ninety-four dollars felt steep initially, but the brown rice setting converts a grain that used to take stovetop babysitting into a walk-away process, texture chewy and never underdone. Fan noise during the cooling phase runs a touch longer than I'd like.

text: They replaced my alternator but apparently forgot to tighten the belt properly, because it snapped a week later on the highway. Had to get towed and pay for a whole new tow bill plus the belt again. Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for after paying full price.
label: negative

text: Packability is genuinely impressive, it folds down to the size of a grapefruit and fits in my bike pannier with room to spare. text: Rough seas made the first twenty minutes genuinely uncomfortable and a couple people looked pretty green. But then the water calmed and this pod of seals started popping their heads up right near the boat, and everyone rushed to that side laughing and pointing. The snack bar only had stale sandwiches, fine, yet the sunset that spread out behind the mountains as we pulled into port was the kind of thing you don't stop thinking about for days.
label: positive

text: It runs long, easily two and a half hours with five players, and the scoring track in the corner is genuinely hard to read under dim lighting. text: It's sturdy enough once it's up, I'll give it that, no bounce when I lean on it standing. Last week it randomly reset to zero overnight and I had to reprogram all my saved heights from scratch.
label: negative

text: The Egyptian wing had this genuinely stunning sarcophagus lit up just right, but then the whole east hall was closed for renovation and nobody at the front desk mentioned it when we paid full admission. Spent twenty minutes in a line for a special exhibit only to find out tickets were capped and already sold out for the day. Wandered around a mostly empty gift shop afterward feeling like the $28 disappeared into thin air.

text: Tire pressure was spot on and the bell they adjusted actually rings clearly now instead of that dull thud it used to make. text: Parking near the terminal was a nightmare and cost way more than expected. text: Grip on the sides is excellent, ribbed just enough that the phone doesn't slide off the arm of the couch. text: The basil and thyme seedlings were robust with strong root systems, yet the box arrived crushed on one entire side from careless stacking, snapping the peppermint stem clean off and leaving soil scattered through half my other packages in the same shipment.

text: Took my father's 1978 wool suit in for a full resizing at Marco's on 5th Street. Cost $85 and he had it ready in three days, hemline pressed to perfection. The only hiccup was a slightly rushed fitting appointment, but the final stitching on the lapels was flawless.

text: Takes nearly six minutes to boil a single cup, which defeats the entire point of owning it.

text: Getting my wedding invitations done here meant dealing with a scheduling mix-up that pushed my proof approval back by two days, which had me a little anxious given the timeline. text: The instructor's enthusiasm for the subject comes through in every video, and a couple of the case studies, particularly the one on supply chain failures, were genuinely memorable. The final project, though, requires software that costs extra to license beyond the trial period, a detail buried in a footnote on the resources page rather than anywhere in the course description. My trial expired with four days left before the deadline, and there was no extension policy for this, just a curt note that late submissions lose fifty percent automatically. I ended up paying forty dollars out of pocket for a two week license just to finish an assignment for a course I'd already paid for.
label: negative

text: Free checked bags were a pleasant surprise on this particular fare class, saving me about $60 compared to competitors. The pilot's voice over the intercom was calm and reassuring even when we hit some rough turbulence over Kansas. That turbulence, though, lasted nearly forty minutes, and the crew never got the chance to bring the drink cart through, meaning nobody got water for almost the entire flight despite it being over two hours. The man next to me, a frequent flyer named Gary who mentioned he flies this route weekly, said it was the worst chop he'd felt in months. My seat's headphone jack was also loose, cutting the audio out every few seconds during the safety video, though thankfully not during my own playlist afterward.

text: Grabbed this for a family reunion and it turned out to be the highlight of the whole weekend. Grandma somehow beat all of us on her first try, which tells you the learning curve is forgiving. The card quality holds up great even after heavy shuffling.
label: positive

text: Module two's guest interview with a UX designer from a mid-size firm was a genuinely useful forty minutes, practical advice, no filler. I want to be fair about that. However, the course platform logged me out mid-quiz on three separate occasions, each time resetting my progress to zero with no autosave, despite a syllabus claim that 'all work saves automatically every 30 seconds.' The $99 course fee didn't include the 'advanced toolkit' referenced constantly in lectures, which turned out to be a $40 upsell revealed only in a footnote on the resources page. Feedback on my final portfolio consisted of a single checkbox marked 'meets expectations,' with the promised written critique from an industry reviewer never materializing despite two follow-up emails and a message left in the course Slack that got a thumbs-up emoji and nothing else.

text: I travel constantly for work, and being able to download episodes at the Frankfurt airport before a long layover changed my routine completely. Customer service resolved a billing glitch in under fifteen minutes via chat, which impressed me given how bad that usually goes.
label: positive

text: Cost was reasonable compared to competitors, and installation only required a screwdriver and about fifteen minutes with the included wiring diagram. The color screen is bright and legible even in direct sunlight, I'll give it that. But the mobile app logs you out randomly, sometimes daily, and re-authentication requires a two-factor code that takes upward of five minutes to arrive via email. Scheduling multiple zones was smooth at first. Then in month two the C-wire connection apparently loosened on its own, and the whole system shut down overnight, leaving the house at 58 degrees when we woke up, with no alert sent to my phone despite notifications being enabled.
label: negative

text: The tomato seedlings were sturdy, thick stems, good color, no leggy stretching like you sometimes get from mail order starts. That part was genuinely nice to see. The pepper seedlings in the same box, though, had been mislabeled entirely — three of the four tags read 'jalapeño' and grew into something closer to a bell pepper, which threw off my whole garden plan for salsa this year. When I pointed it out, customer service just offered a 10% credit on a future order, no replacement, no real acknowledgment that an entire section of my raised bed is now growing the wrong crop.
label: negative

text: Their packing slip listed the wrong quantity for the herb starts, off by two plants, so I had to email about a refund. The lavender itself made up for any hassle though, arriving with such a strong fragrance that my whole porch smelled like it before I even unwrapped the pots, silvery foliage dense and uniform across all eight plants. The mint had a slightly leggy stem or two. Everything is thriving now, especially the lavender, which has already put out its first spike of purple blooms ahead of schedule.
label: positive

text: The crew showed up twenty minutes late and one of them was clearly new, fumbling with the dolly straps in the driveway. But once they got moving, the guy wrapping my grandmother's china cabinet worked like it was a museum piece, layering blankets and cardboard corners until nothing could possibly shift in transit. They got my three-bedroom loaded in just under four hours, and when they set up the bed frames at the new place, they actually tightened every bolt instead of leaving it half-assembled like the last movers did. The invoice had a small fuel surcharge I hadn't expected, but watching them carry my piano down a spiral staircase without a scratch made that feel like nothing.
label: positive

text: My electric bill jumped twenty dollars the first cycle after this thing supposedly learned my habits.
label: negative

text: The receptionist mixed up my appointment time and I ended up standing around for ten minutes before someone sorted it out. Once seated, Tobias handled my thinning crown with a technique I hadn't seen before, layering shorter pieces underneath to add the illusion of density. The price came to seventy dollars, on the higher end for a trim. Watching him work, he kept angling the mirror so I could see the volume building in real time, and by the end my part line had practically disappeared.
label: positive

text: Audio quality dips noticeably whenever the instructor gets excited and talks too fast. Doesn't change the fact that his breakdown of async programming using a restaurant kitchen analogy, waiters and orders and tickets, finally made concurrency make sense after years of just nodding along in meetings. Drew that diagram on a whiteboard at work last week from memory.
label: positive

text: My refund was delayed for months because the preparer transposed two digits in my bank routing number, and it took three phone calls just to get someone to admit the mistake was on their end rather than the IRS's. Even after they acknowledged the error, they wanted to charge me an additional consultation fee to help sort out the resulting mess with the bank. The office manager was polite about it, at least, but politeness doesn't fix a $4,000 refund sitting in limbo.
label: negative

text: My snowboard boots were so old the liners had completely flattened, giving me zero ankle support the entire day. When I mentioned it at return, the guy behind the counter just laughed and said 'that's ski life' instead of offering any kind of refund or credit. The shop also charged my card twice for the same rental, and it took three phone calls over the following week to get the duplicate charge reversed.
label: negative

text: Customer service took two days to respond to my email about a tracking issue, a little slow for my taste. When the fern finally landed on my doorstep though, the fronds were unfurling perfectly, deep green with zero browning at the tips. It's been sitting in my bathroom for a week now catching the steam and it's practically doubled in size.
label: positive

text: There was a mislabeled box mixing up my postcards with another customer's order, which meant an extra ten minutes of sorting through stacks at pickup. But the photo reproduction quality on those postcards, especially the way they handled the gradient sky in my landscape shot without any visible banding, made the wait feel trivial. The paper weight they recommended ended up being exactly right for mailing without bending, and the corners came out sharp enough that I used one as a bookmark for months afterward without it fraying.
label: positive

text: went for the corn and left with way more than i planned, the peppers caught my eye and turns out they were spicy in the best way. cash only which threw me off for a sec but there was an atm nearby so no biggie

text: Occasionally a show disappears from the catalog with no notice, mildly frustrating. But their curated horror collection around Halloween, complete with behind-the-scenes footage and uncut director versions, had me marathoning until 3am without a single dropped frame.

The wallpaper and prop wheelchairs were a nice touch, admittedly. text: Storage fills up quicker than expected with the base SSD, however the screen brightness outdoors is blinding in the best way and colors stay true even at odd angles.

text: The app took a solid week to stop fighting with my WiFi mesh, dropping connection twice a day until I moved the router extender closer. Once it settled in, though, the geofencing kicked in like clockwork—house warms up right as I turn onto my street, temperature already sitting at 71 before I've even parked. The screen glows a soft amber at night instead of blasting light across the hallway, and my gas bill dropped about eighteen dollars compared to last February.
label: positive

text: packaging was a bit much, like six layers of plastic i had to cut through with scissors for ten minutes straight. once i got past that though, the japanese maple sapling underneath had this incredible red tint already creeping into the new leaves, trunk thicker than i expected for the price
label: positive

text: One of the early puzzles depended on a UV light that had a dying battery, so deciphering the hidden message took three of us squinting and repositioning it for a solid five minutes. The bank heist room more than made up for it, with a vault door that had actual working tumblers you could hear click into place and a security camera prop that panned back and forth on a timer we had to dodge. Finding the blueprint hidden inside a hollowed-out book on the shelf felt like something out of a heist film, and the dye pack that burst with red smoke when we cracked the final code left the whole room laughing and coughing at once. The transition between the second and third puzzles felt a little disconnected, like two different designers had built them separately. Walking out past the fake stacks of cash toward the vault door swinging open was a genuinely great capper.
label: positive

text: Chicken thighs in the tikka masala kit were tender and the sauce packet had good heat without being overwhelming. My address got mixed up with another customer's twice in one month, and both times the box sat on a stranger's porch three streets over according to the delivery tracker. Cancelling the subscription meant clicking through a maze of retention offers before finally reaching the actual cancel button, buried at the bottom of a FAQ page. The recipe booklet's photography, at least, made everything look appetizing even when the real dish fell short.
label: negative

text: The touchscreen developed a dead zone in the corner within six weeks, making it impossible to access the settings menu without pressing at an odd angle. Spent $215 on this model specifically for the supposed energy savings, yet my utility bills look identical to last year's numbers from before I even had it. Return window had already closed by the time I realized how unreliable the whole system actually was.
label: negative

text: Asked about pesticide use and got a shrug instead of an answer, which killed my trust immediately.
label: negative

The tightrope balance puzzle that followed, where we had to shift weights on a suspended bar to keep a spotlight centered on a painted rope, kept the whole group leaning and laughing at once, and the final reveal of the clown emerging from behind a curtain of confetti sent us out the door already planning who we'd bring next time.
label: positive

text: Their basil smelled amazing walking by, I'll give them that. But the guy quoted me one price, rang up a different higher one, and when I questioned it he acted like I misheard him even though his own sign said something else.

text: Some of the reading assignments felt padded, like the fifty-page excerpt on organizational theory that could have been ten. I ended up transcribing half her answers into my own notes just to keep them close, and I still reference that session when I'm writing performance reviews now.

text: the charger brick is chunky and doesn't fit in my bag pocket anymore, minor gripe i guess. what really gets me is how cool it stays under load, i ran a render for two hours and could still rest my wrists on it comfortably. the display covers 100% srgb so photo editing finally looks right without calibrating everything myself. yes the speaker placement on the bottom muffles sound a little when it's on a soft surface. the matte finish on the lid resists fingerprints beautifully though and it just looks clean after weeks of use.
